name: APRS: AX.25 UI frames over Bell 202 AFSK 1200
description: T-952: no AFSK1200/AX.25 path existed (docs/06 gap, explorer 2026-09-25). NBFM discriminator -> Bell 202 tone-pair subcarrier (1700 Hz centre, mark 1200 Hz / space 2200 Hz) -> FSK discriminator (deviation 500 Hz) -> 1200 Bd clock recovery -> NRZI decode (transition-is-0) -> zero-bit destuffing over the WHOLE continuous line (bitstuff, T-613, bits mode: flags pass through unstuffed, so this must run before framing -- destuffing an already sync_search-cut frame would misalign every octet after the first stuffed bit) -> flag-delimited HDLC framing (0x7E, terminator the next flag, bit_order lsb: every AX.25 octet incl. the flag is sent LSB first, and by this point the line is destuffed so its octets are aligned) -> CRC-16/X-25 FCS check -> address/control/PID/info fields. sync_search's terminator match keeps the closing flag IN the frame (as ACARS's ETX/ETB does), so crc's span.end_trim_bits=8 locates the FCS eight bits before the frame end, and strip removes only the FCS -- the closing flag (0x7E) stays attached as info's last byte, exactly as ACARS keeps its ETX/ETB, and a consumer trims it (the field map notes it). The flag is only 8 bits (an HDLC design constraint, unlike ACARS's 40-bit sync word), so it chance-matches noise and idle flag runs often; crc's drop_invalid keeps only FCS-valid frames reaching fields/messages. Address octets are ASCII shifted left one bit (each callsign character read as the field's first 7 of 8 bits, the wasted low bit dropped by the length itself); destination/source are kept as raw 56-bit values (hk-recipe's `ascii` field type has no stride/skip option for AX.25's shifted encoding, so callsign text is decoded by the consumer, not this recipe -- see the field map's description). Two addresses only (destination + source, no digipeater path) for a directly-heard beacon.

nodes.label: Bell 202 tone pair (1700 Hz centre) -> baseband
HDLC zero-bit destuff (whole line, bits mode: flags pass through unstuffed)

ax25_frame.description: One AX.25 UI frame after the FCS is stripped: destination (56 bits: 6 shifted-ASCII characters + SSID/extension octet), source (56 bits, same layout), control (8, 0x03 for UI), PID (8, 0xF0 = no layer 3), info (the payload, plain 8-bit ASCII, unshifted). Destination/source stay raw 56-bit values -- each character is ASCII << 1 with an extension bit in the low bit of the SSID octet, which the `ascii` field type cannot express (no per-character stride/skip); a consumer recovers a character as byte >> 1 (equivalently the octet's first 7 of 8 bits) and the SSID as bits 3-6 of the seventh octet.

fields.name: info
fields.label: Information field (APRS payload) -- ends with the closing flag byte (0x7E, '~'), kept attached exactly as ACARS keeps its ETX/ETB; a consumer trims it
